tools.description: Resolve fresh customer-specific AWS, GCP or Azure Cloud Connect prerequisites, identity trust, per-feature permissions, inputs and deployment artifacts. Read-only. Azure management-group requirements return an inline Azure CLI plan/apply script with exact selected roles and a customer binding; it grants access without registering and does not elevate the operator. GCP organization, project and dataset scopes use the returned inline shell artifact. AWS account scopes return the account CloudFormation template and per-account Terraform module. AWS organization scopes return one management StackSet artifact with entrypoint, a flat files list (path, URL and SHA-256 for both templates) and parameters for one root/OU; no fleet connection or rollout operation is created. AWS membership, Organizations/StackSets prerequisites, deployment success and access remain separate checks. AWS organization real-time bucket/enrollment configuration is unsupported by the pinned artifact. Artifacts are reference implementations for adaptation to customer tooling; their requirements and registration behavior remain relevant when adapted. The selected artifact's requirementsSatisfied and findings determine artifact readiness; feature-level flags or preconditions alone do not. Discovery and blocked artifacts have requirementsSatisfied=false and empty parameters. Returned parameters preserve the artifact's exact spelling and structure. Does not enable billing exports. Full Cloud Connect workflow: MCP resource skill://doit-cloud-connect/SKILL.md.

tools.description: Register a deployed AWS IAM role, GCP service account or Azure DoiT enterprise application explicitly when the final deployment does not register it automatically and no connection exists yet. For AWS, retained DoiT Terraform provider resources and CloudFormation callbacks perform registration through their own workflow; an additional registration duplicates that operation. An existing connection for the scope returns 409 connection_exists; changes to that record use a conditional update. Fresh requirements describe prerequisites, and dry_run_cloud_connection_change previews the request. GCP setup scripts grant access but do not register: use descriptor metadata and the selected GCP scope. Azure uses identity.kind azure_service_principal with tenantId and one management-group binding; the live selected grants must carry the setup-written customer binding. The response returns the authoritative connection id, bindingId and registered scope identifiers for subsequent operations. Registration records an existing cloud target; it does not create an account, project, organization or Azure tenant/group. Registration alone does not establish feature readiness or data arrival. Full Cloud Connect workflow: MCP resource skill://doit-cloud-connect/SKILL.md.

tools.title: Dry Run Cloud Connection Change

tools.description: Run fresh synchronous access checks for a registered connection. Results include authentication, per-feature checks and coverage, and `recorded` indicating whether the observation was stored. partial, not_checked and failed checks are not passed; a failed authentication leaves every feature not_checked. AWS declared-policy checks do not prove effective access. GCP checks effective scope permissions; BigQuery dataset results expose sampled table coverage. Azure checks fresh management-group access and unconditional role assignments held by the DoiT application at that exact scope; this does not evaluate every effective permission or deny assignment. Access never proves billing data arrived. Nothing is stored as a run; requestId provides correlation. Full Cloud Connect workflow: MCP resource skill://doit-cloud-connect/SKILL.md.

tools.description: Use this when the user wants a high-level overview or dashboard of their entire cloud infrastructure. Returns cost by cloud provider, top services per cloud, top projects per cloud, recent cost anomalies, and recent cloud incidents — all in a single call. Costs cover the last 30 days including today as totals per cloud, per service, and per project (no daily rows); services and projects are limited to the top 5 values per cloud across that range. Returns at most 5 anomalies and 5 AWS/Google Cloud provider incidents (not account-specific incidents). Failed sections silently return empty arrays, so empty data does not establish zero spend or no incidents. Do NOT use this for detailed drill-downs (use run_query), single-provider analysis, or anomaly-only queries.

Any other key is rejected with an error. Example: 'type:custom|owner:jane@example.com'

tools.name: list_reports
tools.title: List reports

tools.description:
Use this when the user wants to analyze cloud costs, generate a cost breakdown, view spending trends, or run a custom analytics query across their cloud providers. Runs the config through the DoiT Cloud Analytics API query endpoint (https://developer.doit.com/reference/query) and returns the result rows. Accepts a structured config with data source, metrics, dimensions, time range, and filters. Do NOT use this for listing saved reports (use list_reports), checking anomalies (use get_anomalies), or viewing budgets (use list_budgets).
    Unpopulated fields take API defaults: basic cost, last 7 days including today, daily time rows (year/month/day), and billing (or billing-datahub for customers with DataHub metrics).
    Each `config.group[].limit.value` selects top/bottom N dimension values per parent group, ranked across the range; it does not cap result rows and has no tool-enforced maximum of 25. Time columns can produce multiple rows per group.
    `timeRange` covers relative periods; explicit dates require `timeRange: {mode: "custom"}` and sibling `config.customTimeRange: {from, to}`, with no unit.
    For mode "last", "includeCurrent": true includes the current partial period within amount; false selects fully completed periods. One month with true is current month-to-date.
    "metrics" (array) supersedes the deprecated "metric" (object).

    A "group" with id "service_description" and type "fixed" returns a per-service cost breakdown, the most common shape for cost questions.

    Common grouping dimension IDs (all type "fixed"):
      "service_description" — cloud service
      "project_id"          — GCP project / AWS account / Azure subscription
      "cloud_provider"      — cloud provider (AWS / GCP / Azure)

    In default mode "is", filter values must exactly match stored dimension values (case-sensitive): cloud_provider uses provider IDs, while service_description uses service names. Common cloud-provider aliases such as aws/gcp/azure are normalized by run_query. get_dimension({type, id}) returns the valid values for a dimension for this customer.
    Known cloud provider IDs (cloud_provider, type "fixed"):
      "amazon-web-services" = AWS, "google-cloud" = GCP, "microsoft-azure" = Azure

    Example — top AWS services last month:
    {
      "config": {
        "dataSource": "billing",
        "metrics": [{"type": "basic", "value": "cost"}],
        "timeRange": {"mode": "last", "amount": 1, "unit": "month", "includeCurrent": false},
        "filters": [{"id": "cloud_provider", "type": "fixed", "values": ["amazon-web-services"]}],
        "group": [{"id": "service_description", "type": "fixed", "limit": {"metric": {"type": "basic", "value": "cost"}, "sort": "desc", "value": 10}}]
      }
    }

config.description: Configuration for the query. Valid dimension IDs come from list_dimensions or get_dimension.

notTrending.description: Highlight rows that are not trending.

aggregation.description: How to aggregate data values. Accepted values: total, percent_total, percent_col, percent_row.

currency.description: Currency code for monetary values. Accepted values: USD, ILS, EUR, AUD, CAD, GBP, DKK, NOK, SEK, BRL, SGD, MXN, CHF, MYR, TWD, EGP, ZAR, JPY, IDR, AED, THB, COP.

customTimeRange.description: Explicit dates, alongside timeRange (not nested inside it). Required for new custom queries/reports and when switching a saved relative report to custom mode. On update, omitted dates can reuse valid stored custom dates; omitted timeRange requires a stored custom mode. The API uses inclusive UTC calendar days.

from.description: Start timestamp in RFC3339 format, with Z or a UTC offset. The API uses the UTC calendar day.

to.description: End timestamp in RFC3339 format, with Z or a UTC offset. The API includes this UTC calendar day.

dataSource.description: Data source; defaults to billing, or billing-datahub when the customer has DataHub metrics. Accepted values: billing, bqlens, billing-datahub, kubernetes-utilization, attribution. Use attribution for the cost of one attribution: it requires an attribution_tier_1, attribution_tier_2 or attribution_tier_3 dimension in group, dimensions or filters, all from the same attribution (list_dimensions with filter type:attribution_tier_1 lists them). A null tier value is cost no rule attributed.

dimensions.description: Dimensions to break down data by (columns in table view).

id.description: Dimension identifier. Valid IDs come from list_dimensions or get_dimension.

type.description: Dimension type. Accepted values: datetime, fixed, optional, label, tag, project_label, system_label, attribution, attribution_group, allocation, allocation_rule, gke, gke_label, attribution_tier_1, attribution_tier_2, attribution_tier_3.

displaySettings.description: Chart display options for saved reports in the console; no effect on query results. On update, omitted fields keep their stored values.

axisLabelFontSize.description: Chart axis label font size. Accepted values: auto, small, medium, large.

dataLabelFontSize.description: Chart data label font size. Accepted values: auto, small, medium, large.

logarithmicScale.description: Logarithmic value axis (console 'Logarithmic scale'). Applies to line_chart, spline_chart, bar_chart and column_chart only.

numberScale.description: Scale for displayed numbers. Accepted values: auto, thousands, millions, billions, raw.

showDataLabels.description: Show value labels on chart columns, bars and points (console 'Show labels'). Stacked layouts never draw them.

showTotalsPanel.description: Open the series totals panel beside the chart when the report loads in the console (console 'Show totals panel'). Line, area, bar and column layouts only.

themeId.description: Theme ID from list_themes; 'default' clears a stored theme on update.

displayValues.description: How to display values in comparative reports. Accepted values: actuals_only, absolute_change, percentage_change, absolute_and_percentage.

filters.description: Filters to apply to the report.

id.description: The field to filter on. Valid IDs come from list_dimensions or get_dimension.

inverse.description: Set to true to exclude the matched values (negation).

mode.description: Filter match mode. Defaults to 'is' (exact match). Accepted values: is, starts_with, ends_with, contains, regexp.

type.description: Dimension type of the filter field. Accepted values: datetime, fixed, optional, label, tag, project_label, system_label, attribution, attribution_group, allocation, allocation_rule, gke, gke_label, attribution_tier_1, attribution_tier_2, attribution_tier_3.

values.description: Stored dimension values to match exactly in 'is' mode (case-sensitive): provider IDs for cloud_provider, service names for service_description. get_dimension returns available values.

group.description: Dimensions that define rows in the report (group-by).

id.description: Dimension ID for the group-by row. Valid IDs come from list_dimensions or get_dimension.

limit.description: Select top/bottom N values of this dimension per parent group, ranked across the query range. Time dimensions still split result rows.

type.description: Metric type. Accepted values: basic, custom, extended.

value.description: For basic metrics: 'cost', 'usage', or 'savings'. For extended metrics: e.g. 'amortized_cost'. For custom metrics: the custom metric ID.

sort.description: Sort order for the limit ranking. Accepted values: asc, desc, a_to_z.

value.description: Number of dimension values to select per parent group, not a cap on returned rows; time dimensions can produce multiple rows per selected value.

type.description: Dimension type. Accepted values: datetime, fixed, optional, label, tag, project_label, system_label, attribution, attribution_group, allocation, allocation_rule, gke, gke_label, attribution_tier_1, attribution_tier_2, attribution_tier_3.

includePromotionalCredits.description: Include promotional credits. Requires timeInterval of 'month', 'quarter', or 'year'.

includeSubtotals.description: Include subgroup totals. No effect when reading via API. Defaults to false.

layout.description: Report layout / visualization type. Accepted values: column_chart, stacked_column_chart, bar_chart, stacked_bar_chart, line_chart, spline_chart, area_chart, area_spline_chart, stacked_area_chart, treemap_chart, table, table_heatmap, table_row_heatmap, table_col_heatmap, sankey_chart, column_and_line_chart, trend_board, cumulative_comparison.

type.description: Metric type. Accepted values: basic, custom, extended.

value.description: For basic metrics: 'cost', 'usage', or 'savings'. For extended metrics: e.g. 'amortized_cost'. For custom metrics: the custom metric ID.

metricFilter.description: Filter to limit report rows by metric value.

type.description: Metric type. Accepted values: basic, custom, extended.

value.description: For basic metrics: 'cost', 'usage', or 'savings'. For extended metrics: e.g. 'amortized_cost'. For custom metrics: the custom metric ID.

operator.description: Comparison operator. Accepted values: gt, lt, lte, gte, b, nb, e, ne. gt (>), lt (<), lte (<=), gte (>=), b (between), nb (not between), e (equals), ne (not equals).

values.description: Values to compare against.

metrics.description: List of metrics to apply (max 4). Defaults to basic cost on new reports/queries. Non-empty arrays replace stored metrics on update; [] leaves metrics unchanged. Preferred over the deprecated 'metric' field.

type.description: Metric type. Accepted values: basic, custom, extended.

value.description: For basic metrics: 'cost', 'usage', or 'savings'. For extended metrics: e.g. 'amortized_cost'. For custom metrics: the custom metric ID.

secondaryTimeRange.description: Secondary time range for comparative reports.

amount.description: Number of periods to shift back (non-negative).

customTimeRange.description: Custom date range for the secondary time range.

includeCurrent.description: When true, selects complete previous periods (e.g. full previous year). When false, shifts dates by amount.

unit.description: Time unit for shifting. Accepted values: day, month, quarter, year.

sortDimensions.description: Sort order for dimensions. Accepted values: asc, desc, a_to_z. Defaults to 'desc'. No effect when reading via API.

sortGroups.description: Sort order for groups. Accepted values: asc, desc, a_to_z. Defaults to 'asc'. No effect when reading via API.

includeOrigin.description: Whether to include the origin in the split results.

mode.description: Split mode. Accepted values: even, custom, proportional.

id.description: Origin ID.

type.description: Origin type. Accepted values: datetime, fixed, optional, label, tag, project_label, system_label, attribution, attribution_group, gke, gke_label, unallocated.

tools.name: run_query
tools.title: Run Cloud Analytics query

tools.description: Use this when the user wants a simple cost breakdown by service, project, or cloud provider (e.g. 'What are my top services by cost?', 'Which projects cost the most?'). Selects the top-N groups by total cost across the range and returns monthly rows for each. The range includes the partial current month; months=1 means month-to-date. Output row order is not a cost ranking. For complex multi-filter or multi-metric queries, use run_query instead.

cloud.description: Filter to a specific cloud provider. Accepts aliases like "aws", "gcp", "azure".

groupBy.description: Dimension to group costs by. "service" = cloud service, "project" = project/account/subscription, "cloud" = cloud provider.

months.description: Number of calendar months, 1–24 (default 1): N-1 complete months plus the current month-to-date. 1 means current month-to-date.

topN.description: Top dimension values ranked across the range (default 10, max 25). Each value can have a row per month; this is not a row cap.

tools.name: cost_breakdown
tools.title: Cost breakdown

tools.description: Use this when the user wants to see monthly spend over time (e.g. 'Show me my cost trend', 'How has my spend changed over the last 6 months?'). Returns monthly cost data points, optionally broken down by service/project/cloud. The last point is the partial current month; months=1 means month-to-date. For daily granularity or custom time intervals, use run_query instead.

cloud.description: Filter to a specific cloud provider. Accepts aliases like "aws", "gcp", "azure".

groupBy.description: Optional breakdown dimension. If omitted the trend is a single total line.

months.description: Number of calendar months, 1–36 (default 6): N-1 complete months plus the partial current month-to-date.

topN.description: When groupBy is set, select top-N groups by total cost across the range (default 5, max 25), not a row cap.

tools.name: cost_trend
tools.title: Cost trend

tools.description: Use this when the user wants to compare spend between two time periods (e.g. 'Compare the latest three months including this month with January through March'). Period 1 is N-1 full calendar months plus current month-to-date; period 2 is an explicit date range. Returns two separate sets of monthly rows, each independently limited to its top 10 groups across that period. Groups can differ; no difference or percentage change is computed. For more than two periods or advanced comparative analysis, use run_query instead.

cloud.description: Filter to a specific cloud provider. Accepts aliases like "aws", "gcp", "azure".

groupBy.description: Grouping (default "service"): service = cloud service, project = project/account/subscription, cloud = cloud provider. Each period independently selects its top 10 groups.

period1Months.description: Period 1 covers N-1 full calendar months plus current month-to-date, 1–24 (default 3). It is not necessarily a calendar quarter.

period2.description: Comparison period as explicit inclusive UTC calendar dates in RFC3339 format.

from.description: Start timestamp in RFC3339 format, with Z or a UTC offset. The API uses the UTC calendar day.

to.description: End timestamp in RFC3339 format, with Z or a UTC offset. The API includes this UTC calendar day.

tools.name: compare_spend
tools.title: Compare spend

tools.description: Use this when the user asks about optimization, recommendations, insights, savings opportunities, rightsizing, idle resources, security findings, or cost reduction suggestions. Also use this when the user asks 'what insights are available?' or 'show me insights'. This is the primary tool for 'what can I optimize?', 'how can I save money?', and 'what insights do I have?' questions. Returns insights ordered within each page by estimated daily savings, not priority. All statuses are included unless filtered, including dismissed. easyWin is derived from easyWinDescription when present, otherwise null. Follow pageToken for more results. Do NOT use this for cost anomalies/spikes (use get_anomalies) or budget tracking (use list_budgets).

category.description: Filter by one category; a legacy one-element array is accepted. OperationalExcellence/Operational excellence and PerformanceEfficiency/Performance efficiency are filtered within each returned page because the API's category filter cannot match them. An empty page can still have a next cursor.

displayStatus.description: Filter by display status. Omitted means all statuses, including dismissed. Possible values: actionable, acknowledged, in progress, optimized, dismissed.

easyWin.description: True selects easy wins; false selects only non-easy-wins; omit for both.

maxResults.description: Results per page, 1–500. Overrides pageSize; defaults to 20 for compatibility.

page.description: Deprecated: only 0 (first page) is accepted. Use pageToken for continuation.

pageSize.description: Deprecated alias for maxResults (default 20, max 100); maxResults takes precedence.

pageToken.description: Non-empty opaque cursor from the previous response. Omit for the first page.

priority.description: Filter by priority levels. Possible values: Low, Medium, High.

provider.description: Filter by cloud provider (sent as cloudProvider to the API, e.g. aws, gcp, azure).

searchTerm.description: Case-insensitive substring search of insight titles only.

tools.name: list_optimization_recommendations
tools.title: List optimization recommendations

tools.description: Use this when the user wants to see which specific resources are affected by an optimization insight. Returns a page of resourceResults with rowCount and pageToken, resource IDs, accounts, savings or risk counts. There is no dedicated remediation field. Default page size is 1000; follow pageToken for more resources. Do NOT use this for listing all insights (use list_optimization_recommendations).

maxResults.description: Maximum resources per page, 1–5000; defaults to 1000.

pageToken.description: Opaque cursor returned by the previous resource page.

source.description: The source of the insight (e.g. 'aws-cost-optimization-hub', 'aws-trusted-advisor'). Use the 'source' field from list_optimization_recommendations.

tools.name: get_insight_resources
tools.title: Get insight resources

tools.description: Use this when the user wants the details and aggregate summary (savings, risk counts, status, description) of a single optimization insight identified by its source and key. Returns the insight metadata only — it does NOT include the individual affected resources (use get_insight_resources for those) and is not for listing all insights (use list_optimization_recommendations).

source.description: The source of the insight (e.g. 'aws-cost-optimization-hub', 'aws-trusted-advisor'). Use the 'source' field from list_optimization_recommendations.

tools.description: Use this when the user wants to create a new custom insight or update an existing one's metadata (title, description, categories, status, remediation links). Only insights owned by the 'public-api' source can be managed (the default source). Requires key, title, shortDescription, cloudProvider and categories on every call. This replaces insight metadata: omitted optional fields such as detailedDescriptionMdx, reportUrl, easyWinDescription and cloudFlowTemplateId are cleared. Affected resources are managed separately (post_insight_resource_results). For a status-only change, use update_insight_status to preserve metadata despite that endpoint's deprecation.

tools.name: post_insight_result
tools.title: Post insight result

This endpoint is deprecated but remains the safe choice for status-only changes because it preserves optional insight metadata; post_insight_result replaces it. Only insights owned by the 'public-api' source can be managed. When dismissing, dismissalDetails.reason is required; comment is optional. Do NOT use this to edit an insight's title/description or create one (use post_insight_result).

includeCurrent.description: When true, selects complete previous periods (e.g. full previous year). When false, shifts dates by amount.

unit.description: Time unit for shifting. Accepted values: day, month, quarter, year.

sortDimensions.description: Sort order for dimensions. Accepted values: asc, desc, a_to_z. Defaults to 'desc'. No effect when reading via API.

sortGroups.description: Sort order for groups. Accepted values: asc, desc, a_to_z. Defaults to 'asc'. No effect when reading via API.

splits.description: Cost splits to apply to the report.

id.description: ID of the field to split.

includeOrigin.description: Whether to include the origin in the split results.

mode.description: Split mode. Accepted values: even, custom, proportional.

id.description: Origin ID.

type.description: Origin type. Accepted values: datetime, fixed, optional, label, tag, project_label, system_label, attribution, attribution_group, gke, gke_label, unallocated.

id.description: Target ID.

type.description: Target type. Accepted values: datetime, fixed, optional, label, tag, project_label, system_label, attribution, attribution_group, allocation, allocation_rule, gke, gke_label, attribution_tier_1, attribution_tier_2, attribution_tier_3. Must match the split type unless split type is 'attribution_group', in which case target type must be 'attribution'.

value.description: Percent as float (e.g. 0.3 for 30%). Required only when split mode is 'custom'.

type.description: Type of the split. Accepted values: datetime, fixed, optional, label, tag, project_label, system_label, attribution, attribution_group, allocation, allocation_rule, gke, gke_label, attribution_tier_1, attribution_tier_2, attribution_tier_3.

timeInterval.description: Time interval for grouping data (default day). On update, supplying this with dimensions omitted resets time columns to this interval. Accepted values: hour, day, dayCumSum, week, isoweek, month, quarter, year, week_day.

timeRange.description: Time range; defaults to the last 7 days including today on new reports/queries. For custom dates use {mode: 'custom'} and sibling config.customTimeRange.

amount.description: Number of calendar periods (0–5000). Required for 'last'.

includeCurrent.description: For 'last', true includes the current partial period in amount; false (default) selects completed periods. With amount 1 and unit month, true means month-to-date and false means the previous full month. Ignored for 'current' and 'custom'.

mode.description: Time range mode: 'last' selects N calendar periods; 'current' selects the current calendar period through its end; 'custom' requires dates in config.customTimeRange, alongside timeRange.

unit.description: Time unit. Accepted values: day, week, month, quarter, year. Required for 'last' and 'current'; forbidden for 'custom'.

folderId.description: Moves the report to this folder; 'root' moves it to the top level, omission leaves it in place. Folder IDs come from list_folders.

id.description: The ID of the report to update (required).

labels.description: Replaces non-system DoiT console labels; [] clears them, omission preserves them. System labels are rejected.

name.description: Report name.

tools.description: Use this when the user asks to verify their account connection or check who they are logged in as. Do NOT use this for running cost queries directly (use run_query) or viewing allocations (use list_allocations).

filter.description: Filter string in format 'key:value|key:value'. Exact, case-sensitive filters: type and label. Different keys combine with AND; repeated keys are rejected. The API accepts key but it currently matches no dimensions. An empty filter returns an unfiltered page.

pageToken.description: Token for pagination, from a previous response; returns the next page of results.

tools.name: list_dimensions
tools.title: List dimensions

tools.description: Use this when the valid filter values for a specific dimension are needed, such as for a run_query filter, or when the user wants to view dimension details. Returns id, label, type and all available value/cloud pairs in one response, without pagination. For example, get_dimension({type: 'fixed', id: 'cloud_provider'}) returns the exact provider IDs available for this customer. Do NOT use this for listing all dimensions (use list_dimensions) or running queries (use run_query).

id.description: Dimension identifier paired with type, from list_dimensions. For allocation, use the group ID; for allocation_rule, use 'allocation_rule' (the dimension key, not an individual rule ID).

type.description: Dimension type paired with id; use the type returned by list_dimensions. Includes allocation and allocation_rule and legacy attribution types.

tools.description: Use this when the user wants to view their support tickets, check ticket status, or review open issues. Returns tickets with status, severity, and platform. The API cursor and unfiltered rowCount are preserved, including on pages with no matches. Each ticket's fields array lists only custom fields that have a value; unset fields are omitted. pageToken.description: Page token from a previous response; keep the same pageSize when paging.

subject.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the returned API page only. Other pages are not searched. pageToken and rowCount retain the API's unfiltered page values, even when no tickets match.

shared.description: True for a shared channel (omit workspace). Defaults to false at the API.

workspace.description: Connected workspace name returned by discovery. Required unless shared is true; omit it (or pass the empty string discovery returns) when shared is true.

Limit by change filter; a report may configure at most two of `metricFilter`,
`limitByChange` and rank `group` limits. Without `secondaryTimeRange` the change is
a period-over-period delta between adjacent time buckets. With it, each row's
primary-range total is compared with its secondary-range total, so column dimensions
(`dimensions`, which `timeInterval` fills implicitly when omitted) only add buckets
to those totals, while `group` gives every row its own change. A percentage change
is comparable while both periods hold the same number of buckets; an absolute change
is their plain difference and so scales with the bucket count. A row present in only
one range counts as zero there, so a percentage threshold cannot be met from zero. A
percentage-typed custom metric, or count aggregation, is rejected with
`LIMIT_BY_CHANGE_METRIC_NOT_ADDITIVE_WITH_SECONDARY`.

tools.description:
Monitor cost spikes in your cloud environment. Updates the review status of the anomaly identified by `{id}`, the same identifier `getAnomaly` accepts. Mirrors the review workflow available in the console: set `reviewStatus`, and when resolving, qualify it with `resolution` and optionally a `resolutionNote` (feedback reason and comment). The change is recorded in the anomaly's review history exactly like a console update, and the actor is derived from the API credentials - never from the request body.

Validation: `reviewStatus` is one of `NEEDS_REVIEW`, `UNDER_REVIEW`, `RESOLVED`; `resolution` (`ANOMALY_CONFIRMED` or `NOT_ANOMALY`) is required when `reviewStatus` is `RESOLVED` and forbidden otherwise; `resolutionNote.reason` must belong to the given `resolution` - `SECURITY_BREACH`, `MISCONFIGURATION`, `UNINTENTIONAL_PROVISIONING`, `EXPECTED_COST_SPIKE` or `ANOMALOUS_OTHER` for `ANOMALY_CONFIRMED`, and `FAULTY_ANOMALY_DETECTION_MODEL`, `INCORRECT_DATA`, `LOW_IMPACT` or `NON_ANOMALOUS_OTHER` for `NOT_ANOMALY`. Requires the `AnomaliesManager` permission and the `governance:costAnomalies` and `governance:costAnomalies:acknowledgement` entitlements.

tools.description:
Ingest third-party cost, usage, and metric-based data for analysis. Returns one page of the live records of a DataHub dataset, as CSV (default) or as newline-delimited JSON in the same shape as the `/datahub/v1/events` payload.

A time window is required: `startTime` is inclusive, `endTime` is exclusive, and the window must not exceed 366 days. Rows are ordered by their event time and event id, and pages never overlap: read the `X-Next-Page-Token` response header and pass it back as `pageToken` until the header is absent. `X-Row-Count` carries the number of rows in the page. Only live rows are returned; rows deleted through the console or the delete endpoints are excluded.

Every row starts with five provenance columns (`event_id`, `batch`, `source`, `export_time`, `updated_by`) followed by the dataset's business columns in the CSV ingest vocabulary (`usage_date`, `fixed.<key>`, `label.<key>`, `project_label.<key>`, `system_label.<key>`, `metric.<type>`). The business columns are computed from the rows of each page, so consecutive pages can have different label and metric columns; union the headers when concatenating pages. Datasets created with the FOCUS schema template use the FOCUS column names instead and can only be exported as CSV.

To re-import an export into another dataset, drop the `batch`, `source`, `export_time` and `updated_by` columns, and either drop `event_id` or rename it to `id`. This tool returns a JSON envelope with data (the unchanged CSV or JSONL page body) and pageToken (from X-Next-Page-Token). Pass a non-empty pageToken back as pageToken to advance; null means the final page. MCP does not expose the HTTP headers directly.

tools.description:
Access your current and historical billing documents. Returns the PDF document for the invoice specified by the invoice number, including a cancelled invoice or credit memo. The response body is the PDF bytes.
The PDF is returned decompressed by default. It is only gzip-compressed when the request advertises `Accept-Encoding: gzip`, in which case the response carries `Content-Encoding: gzip` with a `Content-Length` for the compressed bytes and must be decoded as a standard `Content-Encoding: gzip` body. HTTP clients whose stack negotiates the encoding automatically also decode it automatically; a client that sets the header by hand may instead receive the raw gzip bytes (for example `curl` decodes only with `--compressed`). Omit `Accept-Encoding` (or send `identity`) to always receive the decompressed PDF. A very large invoice may exceed the decompressed-response size limit and respond with `500`; request it with `Accept-Encoding: gzip` to stream the compressed bytes without that limit.
A `404` is returned both when no invoice with the given number exists for the authenticated tenant and when the invoice exists but has no PDF document available.

tools.description:
Personal notification configs for a user, and organization-wide cost anomaly notifications. Creates an organization-wide notification config. `settings` names one or more public types. Destinations are `emails`, `slackChannels`, and `teamsChannels` arrays. The response returns those three arrays. A channel that a subscribed type does not support is `422` `customers.channel_not_supported`. A Teams destination on a type that supports Teams is `422` `validation_failed` when the tenant has no Teams entitlement.
Requires the `settings` (Manage settings) permission.
The `Idempotency-Key` header is required. The same key and the same body replay the stored success. A different body is `422` `idempotency_key_reused`. A `5xx` response may leave the key reserved, so a retry returns `409` until the original request is released or about 30 minutes pass. `dryRun=true` does not reserve the key. With `dryRun=true` the request goes through the same checks as a real create and returns `200` with `X-Dry-Run: true` and null identity fields (`id`, `createTime`, `updateTime`, `etag`) without creating anything.
Reads are immediately consistent. After a `201`, a GET of that notification returns the created config.

customerContext.description: Scope the request to a specific customer by ID. Required for DoiT employees (whose token isn't tied to a single customer); omit for direct customer users.

destinations.description: Delivery targets for this config. Must include `emails`, `slackChannels`, and `teamsChannels`, with at least one non-empty array.

emails.description: Email addresses that receive the notification, in the order sent. The array is required; an empty array means email is unused. Omitting the array is rejected. At least one of `emails`, `slackChannels`, or `teamsChannels` must be non-empty. Addresses are stored and returned lowercase. A duplicate or an invalid email is `422`.

slackChannels.description: Slack channel ids for Slack channels that receive the notification, in the order sent. The array is required; an empty array means Slack is unused. Omitting the array is rejected. At least one of `emails`, `slackChannels`, or `teamsChannels` must be non-empty. Accepts a public channel, a shared channel, or a private channel the caller is a member of when the DoiT app is also in that channel. A service account cannot add a private channel and receives the same `422` as an id outside the tenant. The caller supplies the id; this API does not look channels up. A duplicate or an id outside the tenant is `422` without saying whether it exists elsewhere. After a channel is accepted, get and list keep returning that id even if the channel is later deleted, archived, or disconnected. That does not mean delivery still works.

teamsChannels.description: Microsoft Teams conversation ids for Microsoft Teams channels that receive the notification, in the order sent. The array is required; an empty array means Teams is unused. Omitting the array is rejected. At least one of `emails`, `slackChannels`, or `teamsChannels` must be non-empty. A duplicate or an id outside the tenant is `422` without saying whether it exists elsewhere. A Teams id is also `422` when the tenant has no Teams entitlement. After a channel is accepted, get and list keep returning that id even if the channel is later deleted, archived, or disconnected, or the tenant loses Teams entitlement. That does not mean delivery still works.

name.description: Display name of the notification (max 200 characters). The stored name is trimmed.

settings.description:
Subscribed notification settings, one property per type. A present property subscribes that type;
`{}` subscribes a type that has no fields. Omitting a property on create leaves that type
unsubscribed. At least one property is required. Unknown properties, including dashboard, report,
and commitment subscriptions, prompt schedules, and `conditions`, are rejected with `422`.

Properties and their Console labels:

- `newInvoices`: New invoices
- `newProformaInvoices`: New proforma invoices
- `paymentReminders`: Due or overdue payments
- `creditUtilization`: Credit utilization
- `quotaUtilization`: Quota utilization
- `cloudIncidents`: Cloud incidents
- `newSkuUsage`: New SKUs usage detected
- `dailyDigest`: Daily digest, one email per selected allocation rule each day
- `weeklyDigest`: Weekly digest, one email per selected allocation rule each week
- `monthlyDigest`: Monthly digest
- `expertInsights`: Third-party insights (Console item "New insights recommended by DoiT experts")
- `insights`: New insights
- `costAnomalies`: Cloud cost anomalies (Console item "Cost anomaly detection")
- `savingsPlanApproval`: Savings Plan purchase requires approval (PerfectScale for Commitments)
- `savingsPlanPurchased`: Savings Plan purchased
- `cudApproval`: committed use discount (CUD) purchase requires approval
- `cudPurchased`: CUD purchased
- `dataIntegrationSyncFailure`: Data integration sync failures
- `awsBillingDataImport`: AWS Billing Data Import Alert

Requires Manage settings; no other permission is checked.

Every destination channel must be supported by every subscribed type, or the response is `422`
`customers.channel_not_supported`:

- Email and Slack only: `expertInsights`, `dataIntegrationSyncFailure`
- Email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams: every other property
- A Teams destination on a supported type is still `422` `validation_failed` when the tenant has
  no Teams entitlement

This API does not list billing profiles, and `GET /billing/v1/invoices` does not return these ids. Empty or omitted means every billing profile in the tenant. A read of an omitted or empty list returns the field absent. An explicit list is returned in the order sent. A duplicate id is rejected with `422`.

costAnomalies.description:
Cost-anomaly notification settings: minimum severity, excess-cost threshold, allocation scope, and
optional resend controls.

allocations.description:
Allocation scope for cost-anomaly notifications. `ids` are allocation ids from `GET
/analytics/v1/allocations`. An id outside the caller's tenant is rejected with `422` without saying
whether it exists elsewhere.

`mode: all` means every allocation with anomaly detection enabled, including anomalies that are not
tied to an allocation, and it carries an empty `ids`. `include` and `exclude` require at least one
id. `mode: all` with a non-empty `ids`, and `include` or `exclude` with an empty `ids`, are rejected
with `422`. `ids` are an ordered list: the server stores and returns them in the order sent, and it does
not sort or drop entries. A duplicate id is rejected with `422`.

ids.description:
Allocation ids, in the order sent. A read returns that same order. A duplicate id is rejected
with `422`. Empty when `mode` is `all`. Non-empty when `mode` is `include` or `exclude`.

mode.description: `all` — every allocation with anomaly detection enabled (and unallocated anomalies). `include` — only the listed ids. `exclude` — all enabled allocations except the listed ids. `all` cannot be sent with a non-empty `ids`. `include` and `exclude` cannot be sent with an empty `ids`.

minExcessCost.description:
Minimum excess cost, as Money. Notify when excess cost is above this amount, not total spend.
`100.00` USD means $100. `currency` must be `USD`; any other currency is rejected with `422`. A
negative amount is rejected with `422`. A fractional amount is rejected with `422` (`100.99` is not a
whole number of dollars). `100` and `100.00` are both accepted. `0` and `0.00` are accepted. Amounts
above 1,000,000,000 whole dollars, and forms such as `Inf`, exponents, a leading `+`, or underscores,
are rejected with `422`. Responses return the amount as `"100.00"`.

amount.description: Decimal monetary amount at ISO 4217 minor-unit precision (string).

minSeverity.description: `warning` — warning and above. `critical` — critical only. There is no `information` or `all` value; a write of `all` is rejected with `422`. Clients may send only `warning` or `critical`. Responses return only `warning` or `critical`. A missing or empty stored severity (console "All severity levels") is returned as `warning`. `critical` is stored and returned as `critical`.

repeat.description:
Resend controls for an active cost anomaly. Omit the whole `repeat` object when neither control is
set. An empty object is rejected with `422`.

everyHours.description: Resend until the anomaly is inactive, every N hours (1–24).

whenCostGrows.description:
Resend when the anomaly's cost grows. At least one of `percentIncrease` or `minIncrease` is required.
An object with only `withinHours`, only `match`, or neither amount is rejected with `422`.

- both `percentIncrease` and `minIncrease` present → `match` is
  required (`or` or `and`)
- exactly one of `percentIncrease` or `minIncrease` present → omit
  `match` (percentage-only or value-only)
- neither amount present → rejected with `422`

`percentIncrease` is an integer percent (`10` means 10 percent) and must be at least 1. Omit
`withinHours` when the time window is off.

match.description: How to combine percent and dollar growth when both are set. Required when both amounts are present; omit when only one amount is present.

minIncrease.description:
Minimum cost growth that triggers a resend, as Money. Must be a positive whole number of dollars.
`150.00` USD means $150. `currency` must be `USD`; any other currency is rejected with `422`. `0`,
`0.00`, and a negative amount are rejected with `422`. A fractional amount is rejected with `422`
(`150.99` is not a whole number of dollars). `150` and `150.00` are both accepted. Amounts above
1,000,000,000 whole dollars, and forms such as `Inf`, exponents, a leading `+`, or underscores, are
rejected with `422`. Responses return the amount as `"150.00"`.

amount.description: Decimal monetary amount at ISO 4217 minor-unit precision (string).

percentIncrease.description: Minimum percent cost increase that triggers a resend. `10` means 10 percent. Must be greater than 0.

withinHours.description: Optional window in hours for the growth check (1–24).

tools.description:
Personal notification configs for a user, and organization-wide cost anomaly notifications. Partially updates an organization notification with an `application/merge-patch+json` body (RFC 7396). Omitted fields stay unchanged; nested objects are deep-merged; nested arrays (for example `allocations.ids`) are replaced when present. When `destinations` is present it replaces the whole destinations object; the nested `emails`, `slackChannels`, and `teamsChannels` arrays are the full lists. Send `null` for a settings property to unsubscribe that type. Nulling the last type is `422`. A channel that a remaining type does not support is `422` `customers.channel_not_supported`. A Teams destination on a type that supports Teams is `422` `validation_failed` when the tenant has no Teams entitlement. Optional resend fields are cleared with `null` (for example `"settings":{"costAnomalies":{"repeat":null}}`). `minSeverity`, `minExcessCost`, and `allocations` cannot be cleared. An id whose config stores a dashboard, report, or commitment subscription or a prompt schedule returns `404`. A settings property that is not on `PatchCustomerNotificationSettings` is `422`.
Requires the `settings` (Manage settings) permission and the `If-Match` header. The `Idempotency-Key` header is required. The same key, the same body, and the same `If-Match` replay the stored success. A different body or a different `If-Match` is `422` `idempotency_key_reused`. A `5xx` response may leave the key reserved, so a retry returns `409` until the original request is released or about 30 minutes pass. `dryRun=true` does not reserve the key. With `dryRun=true` the request goes through the same checks as a real update and returns the notification as it would look after the patch, without changing anything.
Reads are immediately consistent. After a completed update, a GET of that notification returns the new state.

Omitting the array is rejected. At least one of `emails`, `slackChannels`, or `teamsChannels` must be non-empty. Accepts a public channel, a shared channel, or a private channel the caller is a member of when the DoiT app is also in that channel. A service account cannot add a private channel and receives the same `422` as an id outside the tenant. The caller supplies the id; this API does not look channels up. A duplicate or an id outside the tenant is `422` without saying whether it exists elsewhere. After a channel is accepted, get and list keep returning that id even if the channel is later deleted, archived, or disconnected. That does not mean delivery still works.

tools.description:
Read and update your organization's general settings. Partially updates the general settings and contact info of the customer identified by `{customerId}`. `{customerId}` must match the customer resolved from the bearer token; a token scoped to a different customer gets `403`, even if that customer would otherwise be reachable through a reseller/MTS relationship. Requires the `Settings` permission; updating `allowedInviteDomains` additionally requires the `UsersManager` permission.

The request body must use `application/merge-patch+json` (RFC 7396): an omitted field leaves the current value unchanged, and an explicit `null` also leaves it unchanged, except for `urlSlug`, where an explicit empty string removes the customer's active URL slug rather than leaving it unchanged.

Fields are nested exactly as `getCustomer` returns them - `currency` and `allowedInviteDomains` under `settings`, `emails` under `contact` - so every value is read and written at the same path. `settings.currency` accepts only the codes listed in the schema and cannot be cleared; `allowedInviteDomains` and `contact.emails` are cleared with an empty array.

contact.description: Customer point-of-contact details. Shared by the `getCustomer` response and the `updateCustomer` request body so a value is always read and written at the same path.

emails.description: Point-of-contact email addresses for the customer.

customerContext.description: Scope the request to a specific customer by ID. Required for DoiT employees (whose token isn't tied to a single customer); omit for direct customer users.

settings.description:
Customer settings. Shared by the `getCustomer` response and the `updateCustomer` request body so a value is always read and written at the same path.

`currency` accepts only the listed codes; any other value is rejected with `400`. Unlike `urlSlug` and `allowedInviteDomains` it cannot be cleared - no value unsets it.

allowedInviteDomains.description: Email domains allowed to self-invite into the customer. Updating this field requires the `UsersManager` permission in addition to `Settings`. An empty array clears the list.

mfaRequired.description: Whether users of this customer are required to enroll in multi-factor authentication. A missing value is treated as `true`. Disabling this does not remove MFA enrollments existing users already have.

urlSlug.description: The customer's URL display name. An explicit empty string removes the active slug; a non-empty value must be 3-12 characters of lowercase letters, digits, or dashes, starting and ending with a letter or digit, and must be unique across all customers.

tools.description:
Create, view, update, and delete dashboard, report, commitment, alert, and budget subscriptions. This is not Organization-wide notifications. Lists dashboard, report, commitment, alert, and budget subscriptions visible to the caller. Items are ordered by `id` ascending. Nested `subscriptions` are ordered by `type` ascending. `maxResults` defaults to 50. An omitted value, `0`, or a value above 500 is treated as 50. A non-integer `maxResults` is `400`. Pass the response `pageToken` to request the next page. That field is absent when there are no more pages. A `pageToken` that matches no id is `400`. `rowCount` is the total number of subscriptions visible to the caller. That value is the same on every page.
One subscription record is one item. Its dashboard, report, and commitment subscriptions are nested entries that share `recipients`. An alert is one item. A budget is one item. An alert or a budget never shares an item with a scheduled subscription. Draft budgets are omitted. An alert is included only when the tenant has the Governance Alerts entitlement and the caller can view that alert. When the entitlement is missing or cannot be confirmed, the list contains no alerts. An alert with no recipients is still included.
One id namespace is shared by a scheduled subscription, an alert, and a budget. Create accepts only `dashboard-subscription`, `report-subscription`, and `commitment-manager`. Those scheduled types are the resource: create, recipient replace, subscription-set replace, and delete. GET returns alerts and budgets so a caller can see who receives them. Create, delete, and full management of those resources, including recipients, stay on `PATCH /analytics/v1/alerts/{id}` and `PATCH /analytics/v1/budgets/{id}`. PATCH on this API may replace those same recipient lists. DELETE of an alert or a budget returns `409` `customers.entry_is_resource`.
Manage Settings users can view every subscription. A scheduled subscription is also visible to its creator when the caller has the permission for that type, to an owner, editor, or viewer of its source, and to one of its email recipients. Users Manager alone grants no access. A service-account token is evaluated from its own permissions and does not inherit the permissions of the subscription creator. A caller who can see only some nested subscriptions still receives that record; `subscriptions` omits the entries they cannot see. This endpoint is paginated: a response with a non-empty `pageToken` has more results, returned when that value is passed as the `pageToken` parameter. A missing, null, or empty `pageToken` marks the last page.

customerContext.description: Scope the request to a specific customer by ID. Required for DoiT employees (whose token isn't tied to a single customer); omit for direct customer users.

tools.description:
Create, view, update, and delete dashboard, report, commitment, alert, and budget subscriptions. This is not Organization-wide notifications. Creates one dashboard, report, or commitment subscription with one, two, or three scheduled subscriptions: `dashboard-subscription`, `report-subscription`, and `commitment-manager`. Create does not accept `alert` or `budget`. Each type appears at most once. The response is that subscription. Nested entries are ordered by `type`. `name` is `{source name} (Dashboard Subscription)`, `(Report Subscription)`, or `(Commitment Subscription)`, taken from the nested type that sorts first. `createdBy` is the caller.
`subscriptions` must contain one to three entries. A repeated type is `422` `customers.duplicate_subscription_type`. An `alert` or `budget` type, an empty `subscriptions` array, or any server-set field (`id`, `name`, `createdBy`, `etag`, `permissions`, `source.name`, `schedule.nextAt`) is `422` `validation_failed`. `source.id` must belong to the tenant. A missing or foreign source is `422` `validation_failed`. Recipient and schedule value rules are on `CustomerSubscriptionRecipients` and `CustomerSubscriptionScheduleInput`.
The caller must be allowed to manage every sent type: a DoiT employee, Manage Settings, or the permission for that type. Users Manager alone grants no access.
`Idempotency-Key` is required. The same key, caller, customer, method, path, and body replays the stored success response. A different body for that key is `422` `idempotency_key_reused`. A missing key is `400` `idempotency_key_required`. While the first request is in progress, another request with that key is `409` `idempotency_request_in_progress`. A `4xx` response releases the key. `dryRun=true` does not reserve the key. It returns the would-be subscription with `id` and `etag` null and writes nothing.
Reads are immediately consistent. After a `201`, a GET of that id returns the created subscription. The first delivery can take up to an hour.

customerContext.description: Scope the request to a specific customer by ID. Required for DoiT employees (whose token isn't tied to a single customer); omit for direct customer users.

recipients.description: Delivery targets. Both arrays are required.

emails.description: Email destinations in stored order. Reads return each address trimmed and lowercase. Addresses must belong to the organization's approved domains and must be a user or a pending invite. `doit.com` and `doit-intl.com` pass the domain check. A blank email, an email with no domain, or a domain the tenant does not allow is refused with `422` and code `DOMAIN_NOT_APPROVED`. An email that is not a user or a pending invite is refused with `422` and code `NOT_INVITED_USER`. The same email twice, ignoring case, is refused with `422` and code `customers.duplicate_recipient`. An address already stored, and still present, is not checked again.

slackChannels.description: Slack channel ids in stored order. Reads return the public id. Ids are compared exactly after trim. A duplicate id is refused with `422` and code `customers.duplicate_recipient`. A blank or unconnected id is refused with `422` and code `SLACK_CHANNEL_NOT_CONNECTED`. This API does not list eligible channels.

subscriptions.description: Scheduled subscriptions to store on the new subscription. The server sorts them by `type` ascending. Request order is not stored and is not significant. A change of only that order does not write. The response is ordered by `type`, not by this request.

items.description: One scheduled subscription to create. `type` is `dashboard-subscription`, `report-subscription`, or `commitment-manager`, and each type appears once. `attachments` and `pdfSettings` are accepted only when `type` is `report-subscription`. Omitted `attachments` stores `[]`. Omitted `pdfSettings` stores all `true`. A duplicate or unknown attachment value is `422`.

attachments.description: Files to attach to the report email. Report only. Omitted stores an empty list.

items.description: File to attach to a report subscription email. Values may appear at most once. Attachments are email-only: Slack-only subscriptions may still store the choice, and delivery skips the files when there is no email recipient. An oversized file is omitted from that email with a note in the body. This API does not upload or return file bytes.

pdfSettings.description: PDF rendering options. Report only. Omitted stores all `true`.

includeAnnotations.description: Include annotations in the PDF time range.

includeTable.description: Include the data table in the PDF.

showFilters.description: Include the report filters summary in the PDF.

customPeriodAmount.description: Number of `customPeriodUnit` between deliveries. Required when `frequency` is `Custom`. At least 1.

startDate.description: When this schedule starts. The start day is the calendar date of this instant in `timeZone`, not its UTC date. To start on 2026-11-03 in `America/Los_Angeles`, send `2026-11-03T00:00:00-08:00` (`2026-11-03T08:00:00Z`). A read returns the stored instant as UTC RFC3339 (`Z`).

time.description: Delivery clock to store. The value is an instant. A read returns it as UTC RFC3339 (`Z`) and does not preserve an offset. The calendar date is stored and is not the start date. Deliveries use only the hour and minute of that instant, interpreted in `timeZone`.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone for this schedule.

source.description: Source to attach. Must belong to the tenant.

id.description: ID of the dashboard, report, or commitment. Must belong to the tenant. Report ids come from `GET /analytics/v1/reports` and `GET /analytics/v1/reports/{id}`. Commitment ids come from `GET /analytics/v1/commitment-manager` and `GET /analytics/v1/commitment-manager/{id}`. Create checks that id against the customer's dashboards and the preset dashboards.

Create, delete, and full management stay on those APIs. DELETE of an alert or a budget returns `409` `customers.entry_is_resource`.
Manage Settings users can view the subscription. A scheduled subscription is also visible to its creator when the caller has the permission for that type, to an owner, editor, or viewer of its source, and to one of its email recipients. Users Manager alone grants no access. A service-account token is evaluated from its own permissions and does not inherit the permissions of the subscription creator. tools.description:
Create, view, update, and delete dashboard, report, commitment, alert, and budget subscriptions. This is not Organization-wide notifications. Deletes a dashboard, report, or commitment subscription and every scheduled entry on it. Returns `204`. Deleting an id that is already gone also returns `204`, so a retry does not fail. `If-Match` is required when the document still exists; a stale value is `412`. An id that matches no scheduled subscription, alert, or budget returns `204` when `If-Match` is present.
Create does not accept `alert` or `budget`. GET returns them. PATCH may replace their recipient lists. DELETE of an alert or a budget returns `409` `customers.entry_is_resource`.
The caller must have `canDelete` for the subscription. Manage Settings users, a creator with the permission for each scheduled type, and a source owner or editor may delete it. Source viewers and recipients cannot. Users Manager alone grants no access. A service-account token is evaluated from its own permissions and does not inherit the permissions of the subscription creator.
`Idempotency-Key` is required. The same key, caller, customer, method, path, and `If-Match` replays the stored success response. A different `If-Match` is `422` `idempotency_key_reused`. A missing key is `400` `idempotency_key_required`. While the first request is in progress, another request with that key is `409` `idempotency_request_in_progress`. A `4xx` response releases the key. `dryRun=true` does not reserve the key and does not delete.
Reads are immediately consistent. After a completed delete, a GET of that id returns `404`. Two-step: a call with valid arguments deletes nothing. It returns `status: "approval_required"` with a summary of the exact request and a one-time `approvalToken`. The saved request runs only when `confirm_action` is called with that token after the user approves the summary. The token is bound to the caller and expires after 5 minutes.

Create, view, update, and delete dashboard, report, commitment, alert, and budget subscriptions. This is not Organization-wide notifications. Partially updates one dashboard, report, commitment, alert, or budget subscription with an `application/merge-patch+json` body (RFC 7396). The writable fields are `recipients.emails`, `recipients.slackChannels`, and, on a scheduled subscription, `subscriptions`. Any other field, `recipients: null`, or `null` for either recipient list is `422` `validation_failed`. A patch that sets neither `recipients` nor `subscriptions` is `422` `validation_failed`. A wrong `Content-Type` is `415`. Recipient and schedule value rules are on `CustomerSubscriptionRecipients`, `CustomerSubscriptionRecipientPatch`, and `CustomerSubscriptionScheduleInput`.
On a scheduled subscription, `subscriptions` is the desired set of dashboard, report, and commitment subscriptions. A type in the body and not on the document is added. A type on the document and missing from the body is removed. A type in both is updated when `source.id` or the schedule differs, and `nextAt` is recalculated. A stored entry this API does not list stays on the subscription. An empty `subscriptions` array is `422` `validation_failed`; deleting the item is `DELETE`. A repeated type is `422` `customers.duplicate_subscription_type`. An omitted `subscriptions` array leaves the nested types unchanged.
Create does not accept `alert` or `budget`. GET returns them. On an alert or a budget, `subscriptions` is accepted only when it is the one stored entry with the same `type` and `source.id` and no `schedule`. Any other array is `422` `validation_failed`. Those items never gain a dashboard, report, or commitment subscription. Alerts and budgets keep their own APIs for create, delete, and full management. This `PATCH` is the one write this API makes on them, and it may replace their recipient lists. DELETE of an alert or a budget returns `409` `customers.entry_is_resource`.
A patch whose normalized values match the stored values returns `200` and does not write. The `etag` is unchanged.
Recipient changes are allowed when the caller can edit every key on the document, including a key the response did not show. Otherwise they are allowed only when the caller removes exactly their own email: no added address, no Slack change, and no subscription-set change. Any other recipient change is `403`. The caller must be allowed to manage every added or changed scheduled type and to delete every removed type.
`If-Match` must contain the current strong ETag. The token only covers fields this API can write. `Idempotency-Key` is required. The same key, caller, customer, method, path, body, and `If-Match` replays the stored success response. A different body or `If-Match` is `422` `idempotency_key_reused`. A missing key is `400` `idempotency_key_required`. While the first request is in progress, another request with that key is `409` `idempotency_request_in_progress`. A `4xx` response releases the key. `dryRun=true` does not reserve the key. It returns the would-be subscription with the current `etag` and writes nothing.
Reads are immediately consistent. After a completed update, a GET of that id returns the new state.

`100.00` USD means $100. `currency` must be `USD`; any other currency is rejected with `422`. A

1,000,000,000 whole dollars, and forms such as `Inf`, exponents, a leading `+`, or underscores, are
rejected with `422`. Responses return the amount as `"150.00"`.

tools.description:
Beta. Read-only access to Composer recipes and their results. A recipe evaluates your cloud resources against a set of conditions; each result is a finding on one affected resource, and published recipes surface as proprietary Insights in the Console. Returns the Composer recipes that have results in your recently scanned cloud accounts, with counts of those results by status and their estimated savings. Recipes with no such results are not listed. Dismissed recipes are listed with `status: dismissed` and every count set to 0.

Recipes are sorted by `severity`, descending, by default. Ties break by title (case-insensitive), then by `id`.

`filter` is one string of `key:value` clauses: `,` separates alternative values for one key (OR) and `|` separates keys (AND), for example `severity:critical,high|provider:aws,gcp`. Because `,` and `|` are separators, a value itself can't contain them. Supported keys:
- `provider`: one or more of `aws`, `azure`, `azure_ad`, `gcp`, `general`, `google_cloud_source`, `google_workspace`, `k8s`, `oci`, `vmware`.
- `severity`: one or more of `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`.
- `pillar`: one or more of `cost`, `operations`, `performance`, `security`, `compliance`. `compliance` matches recipes tagged with at least one compliance standard.
- `has_active_results`: exactly one of `true` or `false`.
- `allocation`: up to 10 distinct allocation IDs from `GET /analytics/v1/allocations`. Lists only recipes with results on resources in any of those allocations; counts, savings and `rowCount` then cover only those resources. An allocation you can't view returns `404`; if access can't be checked, the request returns `503` rather than unfiltered data.

Requests are always served for the customer your API token belongs to. To list the results of one recipe, use its `id` with `GET /insights/v2/recipes/{recipeId}/results`. This endpoint is paginated: a response with a non-empty `pageToken` has more results, returned when that value is passed as the `pageToken` parameter. A missing, null, or empty `pageToken` marks the last page. Each recipe includes its remediation text, so this tool requests 20 recipes per page unless maxResults is set (the API's own default is 50; pages of 50 or more can exceed the MCP result size limit).

tools.description:
Beta. Read-only access to Composer recipes and their results. A recipe evaluates your cloud resources against a set of conditions; each result is a finding on one affected resource, and published recipes surface as proprietary Insights in the Console. Returns the results of one Composer recipe: one finding per affected resource, with the resource's account, region, tags and cost metrics. An unknown recipe, one your customer isn't entitled to, and a dismissed recipe all return `200` with an empty `items` list and `rowCount: 0`.

By default (`last_scan_only:true`) only results reported by the most recent scan of each recently scanned account are returned. A resolved result keeps the ID of the last scan that reported it, so resolved results rarely appear by default; add `last_scan_only:false` to include them and results from earlier scans. `rowCount` can therefore be lower than the recipe's `totalResultsCount`. Results are sorted by `detection_time`, descending, by default. Ties break by `id`.

`filter` is one string of `key:value` clauses: `,` separates alternative values for one key (OR) and `|` separates keys (AND), for example `region:us-east-1,us-west-2|status:active`. Because `,` and `|` are separators, a value itself can't contain them. Supported keys:
- `account_id`: one or more cloud account IDs, matched exactly.
- `region`: one or more cloud regions, matched exactly.
- `issued_resource_name`: one or more names of the affected resource, matched exactly.
- `related_resource_name`: one or more names of related resources (for example an attached IAM policy), each matched as a substring anywhere in the result's related-resource details.

tools.description:
Manage CloudFlow. Runs a flow once as a test, and **accepts an unpublished (draft) flow** — unlike
`actions/trigger`, which requires the flow to be published. Use this to verify a newly
authored or edited flow before publishing it.

Execution is identical to a production run: the same graph, the same bound connections,
the same credentials, and the same approval behaviour. An approval-gated node still parks
the run and its side effect still waits for a real approval — there is no request that
skips one.

The run is recorded as a test, so it does not appear in run history, does not count
towards dashboard statistics, does not become a dashboard widget's data source, and does
not consume a scheduled-run budget. It does hold the flow's concurrency lock, so a `409`
is returned while the flow is already running.

The flow's first node must be a webhook, scheduled, or manual trigger.

Before dispatching, the flow is validated with the same checks publish applies — a draft
has never been through them. A flow that fails returns `422` listing every offending node
at once, so all of them can be fixed in one pass.

Poll the `Location` URL to follow the run and read what each node produced.

Pass `?dryRun=true` to validate the flow without starting a run. Generated codeNode code may fail silently or error at run time despite passing validation. With dryRun this call shows only that the flow is well-formed; without dryRun it executes real actions even on drafts. A completed run's per-node output (get_cloudflow_flow_run) shows whether it works. The current generated MCP schema exposes no arbitrary trigger payload field; the API uses an empty payload when omitted. Idempotency-Key is required even with dryRun. Same key/request replays within 24 hours; different request fails with 422, an in-progress match with 409. Dry-runs validate existing fingerprints without storing a replay. The API fingerprints MCP tracking parameters; a changed client/server version can cause a same-key conflict. Keep the original request context and key. If an HTTP failure has only generic text, do not infer a status or retry automatically. Full CloudFlow authoring guide: MCP resource doit://docs/cloudflow-authoring.

tools.description:
Manage CloudFlow. Returns a run's status and, for each node, the JSON it consumed and produced. This is how
you find out *why* a run failed, or that it "succeeded" while producing the wrong data.

**`input` is null for most node types, and that is not an error.** Only action nodes — the
AWS, GCP, Azure, Oracle, DoiT and admin operations — record their inputs. Transform, code,
branch, switch, datastore, subflow and trigger nodes record none, so their `input` is
always null. `output` is recorded by every node that finishes, so read a transform's
behaviour from its `output`.

Payloads appear as soon as a node reports a terminal status, so a poll loop can read
results while later nodes are still running.

Any value the node's schema marks sensitive is replaced with a redaction marker;
credentials and connection configuration never appear.

Each `input` and `output` is capped at 64KB. When a payload exceeds that, whole entries
are dropped from the end, `truncated` is true, and `totalBytes` reports the untruncated
size — nothing is silently cut, and what you receive is always valid JSON.

Runs belonging to another tenant, or to a different flow, return `404`. Nodes inside a
fan-out currently report only the last path to finish.

Kubernetes workload cost data measured by the Attribute sensor, and the Attribution Center attributions that split cost into teams, products or customers. Returns one page of rows of Kubernetes workload cost, grouped by `dimension`, for a date
range. Each row has its cost, its change against the previous period of the same length,
and the related values for that dimension (for example the clusters and accounts of a
namespace). Use this for granular rows ("top 10 workloads by cost", "which namespaces grew").

`workloadId`: pass it to the `/attribute/v1/workloads/w/*` operations to see that one
workload's cloud resources.

The request body holds the filters; this operation only reads data. Build filter values
with `listAttributeWorkloadsFilterValues`.

Freemium customers (no paid Attribute plan) see network cost only, and only for the last
60 days.

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Omit `X-Tenant-Id` when the credential
resolves to one customer. When the credential can act on several customers, send
`X-Tenant-Id: <tenant-id>` to select one.

anyOf.description: One condition on one field.

operator.description:
`in` / `not_in`: the field equals / does not equal one of `values` (exact match).
`contains` / `not_contains`: the field contains / does not contain one of `values` as a
substring. `exists` / `not_exists`: the field has / has no value; send `values: []`.

values.description: The values to compare with. Send an empty array for `exists` and `not_exists`.

field.description:
A field to filter on. Get its values from `listAttributeWorkloadsFilterValues`.

- `name`: workload name. `type`: workload type. `namespace`: Kubernetes namespace.

workloadId.description:

`queryAttributeWorkloadsTable`; do not build or change it. An ID that does not decode
returns 404.

tools.name: get_attribute_workload_details
tools.title: Get one workload's identity

tools.description:
Kubernetes workload cost data measured by the Attribute sensor, and the Attribution Center attributions that split cost into teams, products or customers. Returns one page of the cloud resources one workload used in a date range, one row per

`accountability`: the workload's percent of the resource's total cost. Use this for "which
resources drive the cost of workload X". It is the `resource` dimension of

`queryAttributeWorkloadResourcesStats` for totals and the row count, and
`queryAttributeWorkloadResourcesOverTime` for a time series.

decode returns 404. The request body holds the filters; this operation only reads data.

tools.description:
Kubernetes workload cost data measured by the Attribute sensor, and the Attribution Center attributions that split cost into teams, products or customers. Returns three lists of workloads that need attention, grouped by workload name and type.
Each list has every workload that meets its rules, ranked:

- `spike`: cost grew a lot against the week before.
- `new`: workloads first seen in the last two weeks with real cost.
- `network`: network cost grew a lot against the week before (the same rules as `spike`,
  applied to network cost).

The windows are fixed UTC days and do not depend on any date range: the current window is
today minus 8 days to today minus 2 days, and the previous window is the 7 days before it.
`window` and `thresholds` in the response give the exact dates and rules. Use this for
"what changed" or "what should I look at". To get the matching rows or totals over your own
date range, pass `signal=spike|new|network` to `queryAttributeWorkloadsTable`,
`queryAttributeWorkloadsStats` or `queryAttributeWorkloadsOverTime`.

Freemium customers (no paid Attribute plan) see network cost only, so all three lists use
network cost for them.
